label: Person
name: Adam Stanisław Krasiński, Sch. P.
summary:
Adam Stanisław Krasiński (1714–1800) was Bishop of Wilno (Vilnius) from 1762 to 1798 and one of the most politically significant Polish Catholic prelates of the Enlightenment era. A member of the Piarist order (Scholarum Piarum), he was deeply involved in the Polish Enlightenment's educational reform movement, which sought to modernise Poland's institutions before the catastrophic Partitions extinguished Polish statehood.

Krasiński's episcopate at Wilno — the most important diocese in the Lithuanian part of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth — coincided with the First, Second, and Third Partitions of Poland (1772, 1793, 1795). He navigated the collapse of the Commonwealth and the absorption of Polish and Lithuanian territories by Russia, Prussia, and Austria with extraordinary difficulty, attempting to maintain the Church's institutional presence as Poland's political structure disintegrated.

As a Piarist, Krasiński was part of an order whose educational mission had been central to Polish cultural life since the seventeenth century. The Piarists ran schools across Poland and Lithuania, and their educational network was a principal vehicle for the Polish Enlightenment's reform of learning. His combination of episcopal authority and Piarist formation made him both a Church leader and an Enlightenment reformer in one of the most dramatic moments in European history.
